We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have identified a template (733) that disconnections sulfonamide: product -> reactants: Cl-SO2-aryl + aniline (NH2-aryl). The template splits the sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

Our target has sulfonamide linking two aryl groups: a tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonyl, and a phenyl with a side chain (aryl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N: an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which has the side chain.

Thus we can disconnect the sulfonamide: produce sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) where aryl is the tolyl phenyl? Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2... The N attached to sulfonyl is attached to the tolyl phenyl (the N is attached to the tolyl phenyl? Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpret: tolyl ring (Cc1ccc(... )cc1) with substituent NS(=O)(=O) attached to that ring (the N is attached to the tolyl). The sulfonyl group attaches to the other aryl (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonamide is between the tolyl amine (aniline) and the sulfonyl attached to the second aryl.

Thus disconnection: tolyl aniline (p-toluidine) + sulfonyl chloride of second aryl (ClSO2-aryl2). Then later we need to make the aryl2 sulfonyl chloride from the aryl2 (which contains the side chain). The side chain includes an amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). That is an anilide with an extra amino group on the phenyl (para-? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH2 at para? It's an aniline with an amino group at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with two amino groups? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (the first N is the amide nitrogen). The second N is attached to the aromatic carbon as substituent (aniline). So it's a 1,4-diaminobenzene? Not exactly; but we can treat as an aniline (para-aminophenyl) attached via amide.

Thus we need to form the amide: C=CH-CO-NH-aryl (aniline). This could be formed via amide coupling of acryloyl chloride with aniline (para-aminophenyl). Or via condensation of acryloyl acid with aniline.

Simplify: propose retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide using template 733: target -> p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) + aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)

Check buyability: p-toluidine is buyable (we saw True). The aryl sulfonyl chloride likely not buyable (we saw false). So need to make that sulfonyl chloride in step 2.

Step 2: Disconnection of sulfonyl chloride from aryl: we can get aryl sulfonic acid (HO-SO2-aryl) then convert to chloride via thionyl chloride. But we need a template for sulfonyl chloride formation from sulfonic acid? Not sure.

Alternative: we can start from aryl sulfonic acid (aryl-SO3H) which may be commercially available? Not sure. Could also start from aryl sulfonyl chloride directly via chlorination of sulfonic acid.

But maybe we can disconnect the side chain: the aryl sulfonyl chloride can be made from the aryl (c2ccc(... )cc2) with sulfonyl chloride substituent. That aryl could be obtained via sulfonylation of the aryl with chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H) to give aryl sulfonyl chloride. That's a known reaction: aromatic sulfonyl chloride synthesis via chlorosulfonation of aromatic ring. So we can consider step 2: aryl (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2) + chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H) -> aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we need aryl precursor: the phenyl ring bearing the side chain but no sulfonyl. That is c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (a phenyl with a cinnamoyl anilide side chain). This could be made via Suzuki coupling? Actually it's a simple phenyl with side chain attached at para position? The side chain is attached via a carbon (aryl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aryl). That's a styryl amide. Could be formed via Heck coupling of an aryl bromide with acrylamide? Or via Wittig? Simpler: start from 4-bromo phenyl (or 4-iodo phenyl) and do Heck coupling with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). Or we could start from 4-vinyl phenyl (styrene) and do oxidation then amide formation.

But we have limited steps (max 3). So we need to keep route simple.

Potential route:

Target -> Step1: sulfonamide formation (template 733) between p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Step2: aryl sulfonyl chloride from aryl (phenyl with side chain) via chlorosulfonation (ClSO3H). This is a single-step functional group transformation (adds SO2Cl). Not a template but we can treat as a reaction.

Step3: the aryl with side chain can be made via Heck coupling of 4-bromo phenyl (or 4-iodophenyl) with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). The acrylamide can be made from acryloyl chloride + aniline (para-aminophenyl). That could be step 3? But we already have 3 steps max. So we need to combine.

Alternative: Use amide formation as step 3: start from acryloyl chloride + 4-aminophenyl (para-aminophenyl) to give the side chain amide (C=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). Then do Heck coupling with 4-bromo phenyl to attach to aryl. That's two steps already (amide formation + Heck). Then sulfonylation + sulfonamide formation would be 4 steps.

We need max 3 steps. Maybe we can combine steps: Use a known commercial aryl sulfonyl chloride that already has the side chain? Not likely.

Maybe we can use a template that directly forms the sulfonamide from p-toluidine and a phenyl with side chain and SO2Cl? That's step1 only. So we need to get the aryl sulfonyl chloride in one step from a commercially available aryl sulfonic acid (maybe available). Check buyability of aryl sulfonic acid with side chain: "O=S(=O)(O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1". We checked earlier not buyable.

Maybe we can use a different disconnection: break the amide bond instead of sulfonamide. Use amide formation between the side chain carbonyl and aniline. That would give two fragments: acryloyl chloride (or acryloyl acid) and aniline (para-aminophenyl). The acryloyl chloride is cheap and buyable. The aniline is buyable. Then we need to attach the aryl sulfonyl part to the acryloyl? Wait the amide is attached to the side chain phenyl, not to the sulfonyl phenyl. So we could disconnect the amide: target -> aryl sulfonyl phenyl (c2ccc(SO2NH... )cc2?) Actually the amide is on the side chain phenyl (Nc3ccccc3N). So disconnect amide: we get acryloyl chloride + aniline (para-aminophenyl). The rest of molecule is the aryl sulfonyl phenyl with a vinyl group (C=C) attached to the carbonyl carbon? Actually after amide formation, the acryloyl part is attached to the phenyl via the carbonyl, and the double bond is attached to the aryl sulfonyl phenyl via the vinyl group. So after disconnecting amide, we have a fragment: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/)cc2)cc1 (aryl sulfonyl phenyl with vinyl). This fragment still contains the sulfonamide and the vinyl attached to the aryl2.

We could then disconnect the sulfonamide as before, giving p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride with vinyl substituent. Then we need to make the vinyl aryl sulfonyl chloride from the aryl with vinyl (c2ccc(/C=C/)cc2). That could be made via chlorosulfonation of the vinyl phenyl (commercial). Vinyl phenyl (4-vinyl phenyl) is commercially available (p-vinyltoluene? Actually 4-vinyl phenyl). The vinyl phenyl is "c1ccc(C=C)cc1". That is commercially available. Then chlorosulfonation gives sulfonyl chloride with vinyl substituent. Then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine gives intermediate (aryl sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine). Then amide formation with acryloyl chloride + para-aminophenyl gives final product? Wait order: we need to attach the side chain amide to the vinyl phenyl before sulfonamide? The vinyl phenyl after sulfonylation still has vinyl group; the amide attaches to the vinyl carbonyl after oxidation? Actually the vinyl group is part of the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the vinyl is attached to carbonyl (acrylamide). So the vinyl phenyl is the aryl that will be attached to the carbonyl carbon via a double bond. So we need to form the α,β-unsaturated amide after sulfonylation? The sulfonylation does not affect the vinyl. So we could first sulfonylate the vinyl phenyl to get sulfonyl chloride with vinyl. Then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine gives sulfonamide product with vinyl phenyl attached to sulfonyl. Then we need to convert the vinyl to the α,β-unsaturated amide by reacting with acryloyl chloride? Actually the vinyl is already part of the side chain: the vinyl carbon is attached to the carbonyl carbon of the amide. So we need to attach the carbonyl and amide to the vinyl carbon. That is a Michael addition? Actually the structure is aryl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aryl-NH2. So the vinyl carbon is attached to carbonyl carbon (C=O) via a double bond (conjugated). This is an acryloyl group attached to aryl via the β-carbon. So we could form this by Heck coupling of aryl bromide with acryloyl chloride? Not exactly.

Better: start from aryl sulfonyl chloride with vinyl (aryl-CH=CH2). Then perform a carbonylation (oxidation) to convert vinyl to acrylamide? Could be hydroformylation then oxidation then amide formation, too many steps.

Given constraints, maybe we can propose a 3-step route using known reactions but not necessarily using templates. The problem likely expects using template 733 for sulfonamide formation, and another template for amide formation (maybe template 401931? but that seems not appropriate). We can search for amide formation template.

Search for functional_groups_formed "amide" and functional_groups_broken "acyl chloride". Already did, got some templates. Template 884884 seems to involve amide formation from acyl chloride and amine with double bond? It shows product: [CH2]=[CH]C(=O)N... So that could be used.

Thus step 2: amide formation between acryloyl chloride and aniline (para-aminophenyl). Use template 884884 (retro_smarts: ...). Check matching.

Check if acryloyl chloride SMILES: C=CC(=O)Cl. Use check matching with template 884884.
